metric.why: Annual matching and hourly matching are very different claims; hourly carbon-free matching is the harder standard the largest operators now report progress against. Reading which claim is being made matters more than the percentage.
metric.definition: The share of facility consumption matched by renewable generation, reported either as annual matching through purchased certificates or as around-the-clock hourly matching.

reading.body:
Renewable energy utilization percentages from data centers are not comparable unless the matching method is the same: annual certificate matching and hourly carbon-free matching are fundamentally different claims, and the percentage matters less than which standard is being used.

Annual matching lets an operator buy renewable certificates anywhere in the grid, at any time of year, to offset total consumption on paper. Hourly matching requires that clean generation cover consumption in the same hour it occurs, which is far harder to achieve and far more meaningful as a measure of actual grid impact. The largest operators now report progress against the hourly standard, which is why that standard is the relevant benchmark when comparing facilities.

What this metric does not reveal is the absolute energy volume behind the percentage, the physical location of the matched generation relative to the facility, or whether surplus renewable capacity was built specifically to serve data center load. Those factors determine whether a high utilization figure represents a genuine reduction in fossil generation or an accounting exercise. Renewable energy utilization sits alongside water and carbon effectiveness metrics, but none of the three alone describes how a facility's power demand shapes the grid it draws from.
